text: キングスムーアFCとウェストポートアルビオンの試合は3-3の熱戦に。キングスムーアのヴィクター・クインランは8分のPK（得点確率76%）で同点にし、12分にも別のチャンスを決めました[#152][#222]。ウェストポートはラファエル・ドラクロワが22分と30分に高確率（77%と97%）で連続ゴール[#401][#553]。51分にはケンジ・ラーマンが同点弾を決め、試合を振り出しに戻します[#983]。81分にキングスムーアは退場者を出しましたが、82分にルカ・イバーセンが素早いクロスから決め寄せました[#1495][#1516]。両チームともボール保持やパス精度は互角、戦術はキングスムーアが広い場所からのクロス重視、ウェストポートは縦に早いパスで攻め合いとなったゲームでした[#1187][#1459]。

trace.output: Brief: full-match recap for fan audience in ja

- Viktor Quinlan scored 2 goals for Kingsmoor FC, including a penalty at 8' with xG 0.76 and an open play goal at 12' with xG 0.266 [#152, #222].  
- Rafael Delacroix scored twice for Westport Albion at 22' and 30' with high xG values of 0.768 and 0.973 respectively [#401, #553].  
- Kenji Rahman equalized for Westport Albion at 51' with xG 0.693 to make it 2-2 [#983].  
- Luca Iversen scored at 82' for Kingsmoor FC with xG 0.868, reducing the deficit to 3-2 [#1516].  
- Felix Barros received a red card (second yellow) for Kingsmoor FC at 81', impacting the team's defense before the final stages [#1495].

- Kingsmoor FC’s opening goal came from a penalty converted by Viktor Quinlan after a direct set-piece opportunity, showing their ability to capitalize on opponents' fouls in wide areas typical for a 4-4-2 wide crossing style [#152].  
- Their second goal resulted from an 8-pass buildup over 27 seconds initiated by a regain, indicating effective ball retention and progression through wide midfielders and fullbacks involved in crossings (Felix Duarte assisting), consistent with their wide, crossing-focused 4-4-2 formation [#222].  
- Westport Albion’s goals involved quicker, vertical passing sequences starting from regains and rapid direct attacks as evidenced by Rafael Delacroix’s first two goals assisted by short and cross passes within 10 and 40 seconds respectively, reflecting their direct, vertical passing style and 4-4-2 setup aiming to exploit quick transitions [#401, #553].  
- The equalizer by Kenji Rahman came after a short passing sequence starting from a throw-in, progressing through midfield and delivered as a cross, showing a mixture of short buildup and crossing, possibly a slightly adjusted tactical phase fitting Westport’s direct style but utilizing width [#983].  
- Kingsmoor’s late goal came from a quick 2-pass buildup after a ball regain, finished by a low cross assist from Mason Morales, reinforcing Kingsmoor’s pattern of relying on wide players to deliver crosses into the box typical for their wide 4-4-2 formation and crossing style [#1516].  
- Tactical changes by Kingsmoor to press higher and play more direct under coach Pablo Iriarte after falling behind show a shift to increase ball recoveries and chance creation by intensifying pressing and increasing directness, decreasing possession but emphasizing quick vertical transitions aligned with their crossing style [#1187].  
- Westport’s later tactical adjustment to drop deeper, reduce pressing and slow tempo, aiming to protect the lead, aligns with a more cautious 4-4-2 defensive block, reducing opponents’ space and risks, while accepting less ball recovery high up and fewer box touches [#1459].  
- High turnovers and PPDA values indicate Kingsmoor pressed less aggressively in the first half (ppda 10.8) compared to Westport’s more intense pressing (ppda 6.8), consistent with Westport’s vertical direct approach seeking ball recoveries higher up; this dynamic shifted somewhat after tactical changes [#team_stats].
